question: What is the primary purpose of planning in community health nursing?

options.A: To replace the need for physical nursing assessments
options.B: To bridge current health deficits and future outcomes proactively
options.C: To guarantee unlimited financial funding from the government
options.D: To eliminate the need for community participation

explanation: Planning acts as a systematic bridge that moves healthcare delivery from reactive crisis management to proactive, sustainable interventions aimed at desired health outcomes. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h1)

question: Why is early community engagement vital during the planning phase in Nigeria?

options.A: It fosters community ownership and improves health program uptake
options.B: It shifts all financial responsibilities entirely onto the villagers
options.C: It removes the need for professional nursing documentation
options.D: It prevents the government from inspecting local clinics

explanation: Engaging community members early fosters a sense of ownership, which significantly improves the success and uptake of public health initiatives. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h1)

question: Which term best describes the nature of the community health planning cycle?

options.D: A random series of emergency responses

explanation: The planning cycle is continuous and iterative, meaning lessons from evaluation feed back into assessment for ongoing improvement. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: What is the immediate consequence of a flawed situational analysis phase in the planning cycle?

options.A: Subsequent priorities and action plans will fail to target true needs
options.B: The community will automatically receive excess funding
options.D: National health policies will be rewritten

explanation: Because each phase builds on the previous one, an inaccurate assessment leads to ineffective priority setting and action planning. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: What type of need is defined and measured by health professionals based on established standards?
explanation: Normative needs are those defined and determined by health professionals and experts based on clinical or epidemiological standards. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h3)

question: Why is it important for a needs assessment to identify community assets alongside health deficits?

options.A: To eliminate the need for government intervention entirely
options.B: To find local entry points and resources like youth groups or traditional leaders
options.C: To fulfill legal requirements for tax exemption
options.D: To increase the cost of implementing health programs

explanation: Uncovering community strengths and assets helps identify valuable local entry points, such as groups and leaders, to support future interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h3)

question: Why is prioritization necessary in community health nursing planning?

options.A: Resources such as time, money, and personnel are always limited
options.B: Communities usually experience only one health problem at a time
options.C: Ministry guidelines forbid tackling more than one disease a year
options.D: It replaces the need for data collection

explanation: Because healthcare resources are limited, prioritization is necessary to decide which issues require immediate, impactful action. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h4)

question: Which of the following is a standard criterion used to prioritize public health problems?

options.A: The personal preference of the youngest nurse on duty
options.B: The magnitude and severity of the health problem
options.C: The complexity of medical jargon required
options.D: The distance from the capital city

explanation: Magnitude (how many are affected) and severity (mortality/morbidity) are core public health criteria for ranking problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h4)

question: What factor must a community health nurse prioritize when selecting a health intervention strategy in Nigeria?

options.A: Adherence to local realities, cost-effectiveness, and cultural acceptability
options.B: Using the most expensive high-tech equipment available globally
options.C: Ensuring the strategy requires no community involvement
options.D: Focusing solely on international clinical trials

explanation: Interventions must be practical, cost-effective, and culturally acceptable within the local Nigerian context to succeed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h5)

question: Why is consulting established Ministry of Health guidelines important during strategy selection?

options.A: It ensures the chosen interventions are evidence-backed and policy-compliant
options.B: It eliminates all forms of community disease permanently
options.C: It removes the need for nursing documentation
options.D: It guarantees an immediate increase in hospital beds

explanation: Referencing national and international guidelines ensures that interventions are scientifically sound and aligned with established health policies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h5)

question: What does the 'M' in SMART objectives stand for?
explanation: In SMART criteria, 'M' stands for Measurable, ensuring that progress and outcomes can be quantified. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h6)

question: What is the primary function of an action plan in community health nursing?

options.A: To list what needs to be done, who will do it, and when
options.B: To replace the community diagnosis report
options.C: To serve as a legal contract for patient employment
options.D: To calculate annual national inflation rates

explanation: An action plan translates strategies into concrete operational tasks, assigning roles, timelines, and responsibilities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h6)

question: What should a community health nurse do when government funding is inadequate for a health plan?

options.B: Engage in resource mobilisation through partnerships, local assets, and NGOs
options.C: Purchase all required materials using personal salary
options.D: Ignore the shortage and proceed without any supplies

explanation: When government funds fall short, nurses utilize resource mobilisation by partnering with NGOs, leveraging community contributions, and seeking local support. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h7)

question: What does resource allocation primarily involve in community health planning?

options.A: Distributing available assets efficiently and equitably across planned activities
options.B: Hiding medical supplies in storage rooms to prevent theft
options.C: Transferring all community health clinics to urban centers

explanation: Resource allocation is the efficient and equitable distribution of human, financial, and material assets to execute planned activities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h7)

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is routine day-to-day tracking, while evaluation is a periodic assessment of overall objectives
options.B: Monitoring is done only at the end of a project, while evaluation is done daily
options.C: Monitoring deals with finances only, while evaluation deals with patient medications
options.D: There is no functional difference between the two terms

explanation: Monitoring involves ongoing daily tracking of activities, whereas evaluation is a periodic assessment of whether objectives and impact were achieved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h8)

question: Why is formative evaluation particularly valuable during a community health intervention?

options.A: It allows the team to make mid-course corrections while the program is running
options.B: It permanently closes down the clinic once goals are met
options.C: It removes the need for community participation
options.D: It calculates the exact budget for the next ten years

explanation: Formative evaluation happens during the program, enabling nurses and teams to make necessary adjustments and mid-course corrections. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h8)
